\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{نظریہ} (nazariyā)}{نظریہ (nazariyā)}]{\ur{نظریہ} (nazariyā) — a theory}

\label{lesson:UR-C353-nazariya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for knowledge, then the Urdu for to pick out.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{نظریہ}}
\textbf{\ur{نظریہ}} — \emph{nazariyā} — \textquotedblleft{}a theory\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{یہ} \ur{نظریہ} \ur{ابھی} \ur{ثابت} \ur{نہیں} \ur{ہوا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yih nazariyā abhī sābit nahīṅ huā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This theory has not been proved yet.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{نظریہ}} (\emph{nazariyā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{naẓariyya}, \textquotedblleft{}a theory\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{naẓar}, \textquotedblleft{}looking, consideration\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nazariyā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nazariyā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yih nazariyā abhī sābit nahīṅ huā.} — This theory has not been proved yet.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for knowledge, then the Urdu for to pick out, then say \emph{nazariyā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{نظریہ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A theory\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

Before the new one: say the Urdu for to pick out, then the Urdu for a theory.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ٹکنا} (ṭiknā)}{ٹکنا (ṭiknā)}]{\ur{ٹکنا} (ṭiknā) — to hold up; to last}

\label{lesson:UR-C353-tikna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for an exception, then the Urdu for real.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ٹکنا}}
\textbf{\ur{ٹکنا}} — \emph{ṭiknā} — \textquotedblleft{}to hold up; to last\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{یہ} \ur{نظریہ} \ur{عمل} \ur{میں} \ur{نہیں} \ur{ٹکتا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yih nazariyā amal meṅ nahīṅ ṭiktā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This theory does not hold up in practice.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{مکان} \ur{طوفان} \ur{میں} \ur{ٹکا}, \emph{voh makān tūfān meṅ ṭikā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ٹکنا}} (\emph{ṭiknā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{ṭiknā}, \textquotedblleft{}to stop, to remain\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{*ṭakk}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 5420).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{منوانا} (manvānā)}{منوانا (manvānā)}]{\ur{منوانا} (manvānā) — to win acceptance for; to get (someone) to accept}

\label{lesson:UR-C353-manvana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for real, then the Urdu for to hold up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{منوانا}}
\textbf{\ur{منوانا}} — \emph{manvānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to win acceptance for; to get (someone) to accept\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{اپنی} \ur{بات} \ur{سب} \ur{سے} \ur{منوائی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{us ne apnī bāt sab se manvāī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She got everyone to accept her point.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{اپنی} \ur{بات} \ur{منوائی}, \emph{us ne apnī bāt manvāī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{منوانا}} (\emph{manvānā}) is the causative of \emph{mānnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to accept, to obey\textquotedblright{}, which is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{mānnā} under Sanskrit \emph{mányate}, \textquotedblleft{}thinks\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 9857).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{manvānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{manvānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{us ne apnī bāt sab se manvāī.} — She got everyone to accept her point.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for real, then the Urdu for to hold up, then say \emph{manvānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
